claim: Every 2-matroid of rank at most four has an ultra log-concave product-weighted rank sequence. The result now has an analytic proof; the enumeration recorded here is corroboration.
axiom: For feasible S,T with |T| >= |S|+2, some x in T minus S makes S union {x} feasible.
analytic_reduction: All conditional antipodal-pairs inequalities reduce to ground sets of size two, four or six. All three cases now have analytic proofs. The six-element argument imports the main graph APU theorem and is documented in rank_four_analytic_proof.md.
enumeration_role: Independent exact finite cross-check; not a dependency of the current analytic proof.
arithmetic: exact integers and bit masks; no floating-point comparisons
scope: All nonempty families Q of four-subsets of six labelled elements, all triple families T containing the triple shadow of Q, and the uniquely derived maximal permitted pair family P_max(Q,T).
dependencies: C++17 compiler supporting __builtin_popcount, standard library, documented analytic reduction, Kahn-Neiman CAPP-to-ULC theorem
limitations: This does not establish the unrestricted-rank 2-matroid conjecture. Both the main singleton-and-pair theorem and the rank-four extension now have analytic proofs. No independent historical-priority claim is made for the supplementary result.
